Meaning of a 5 A fuse rating; the fuse clause of C 2.5-LO-2.
Tungsten for the bulb filament; the filament-lamp clause of C 2.5-LO-2.
Defines electric energy; the energy clause of C 2.5-LO-1.
Defines electric power; verbatim C 2.5-LO-1.
The product of p.d. and current is power; C 2.5-LO-1.
SI unit of electric power; C 2.5-LO-1.
Unit in which electrical energy is sold, i.e. the kilowatt hour; C 2.5-LO-1.

Kilowatt versus kilowatt hour is the power/energy distinction; C 2.5-LO-1.

Differences between a voltmeter and an ammeter; the instrument clause of C 8.1-LO-5.
Defines a circuit and contrasts open with closed. No symbols or meter readings are asked for, so this stays at the competency rather than C 8.1-LO-5.

Second symbol-identification item; the standard-symbols clause of C 8.1-LO-5.

Factors affecting resistance with the expression; verbatim LO-3.

Copper versus manganin of equal length and resistance: the lower-resistivity wire is thinner. Verbatim LO-3.
A potential difference is the condition for charge to move, maintained by a cell; LO-1 relates p.d. to current.
Thicker wire means lower resistance (LO-3) and the question is answered as a predicted ammeter reading (C 8.1-LO-5).
Longer wire means higher resistance (LO-3), again answered as a predicted ammeter reading (C 8.1-LO-5).
Matches V-I graph slopes to R1 > R2; Ohm's law read graphically. No combination is involved, so not LO-2.
Judges whether a drawn circuit is correctly connected; the circuit-diagram outcome.
Resistance versus resistivity; the distinction sits inside LO-3, which relates resistance to material.

Salient features of series and parallel combinations (LO-2) together with an explicitly demanded pair of drawn diagrams (C 8.1-LO-5).

Copper and aluminium for transmission because of low resistivity; the material clause of LO-3.
Nichrome for an iron's heating element; the heater clause of C 2.5-LO-2.
Two immersion heaters heat faster in parallel because the combined resistance is lower (LO-2) and heat follows from that (C 2.5-LO-2).
Defines the kilowatt hour and relates it to the joule; verbatim the kWh clause of C 2.5-LO-1.

Experiment on the factors affecting resistance; verbatim LO-3.
Joule's heating effect and its everyday applications; verbatim C 2.5-LO-2. Duplicate of the applications half of qid:86971.
Unit of e.m.f. is the volt; potential difference in LO-1.
The kilowatt hour is a unit of energy; C 2.5-LO-1.
1 kWh in joules; the kWh clause of C 2.5-LO-1.
Materials that carry larger currents are conductors, a classification by resistivity; the material clause of LO-3.
Conventional direction of current; a convention about current rather than the V-I-R relation.
Unit of specific resistance, i.e. resistivity; LO-3.

Commercial unit of electrical energy; the kWh clause of C 2.5-LO-1.

P = VI for a bulb at 220 V and 0.5 A; the power outcome.
Order of magnitude of insulator resistivity; the material clause of LO-3.
1 kWh in joules; the kWh clause of C 2.5-LO-1.
Resistance of insulators is very high, a material classification; LO-3.
Resistivity depends on the material only; verbatim LO-3.
Number of 6 ohm resistors needed to make 2 ohms; equivalent resistance in parallel.

Free electrons make a metal a conductor, a material classification; LO-3.
Current through one branch of a drawn network; needs the equivalent resistance of the combination. The figure is not stored, so the item is unanswerable as held.
Compares filament resistances of a 40 W and a 60 W lamp at 220 V through R = V squared / P; the power outcome.
